related_questions.question: What is the inflation rate in Canada history?

text_blocks.snippet: The Canadian inflation rate has fluctuated significantly throughout history, with periods of high inflation following major events like World War I and the COVID-19 pandemic. In recent decades, Canada has generally maintained a low and stable inflation rate, targeted around 2%, but experienced a surge in 2022 due to increased demand and supply chain disruptions. As of June 2025, core inflation is at 2.70%.
snippet_highlighted_words: As of June 2025, core inflation is at 2.70%

list.title: Early 20th Century:
list.snippet: Inflation reached a high of 21.6% in June 1920, followed by a period of deflation with -17.8% in June 1921, according to Trading Economics.

list.title: Post-World War II:
list.snippet: Inflation remained relatively low and stable for several decades, averaging around 2% for 25 years until the COVID-19 pandemic.

list.title: Recent Decades:
list.snippet: The Bank of Canada has successfully kept inflation close to 2% for a long period.

list.title: COVID-19 Pandemic:
list.snippet: In 2022, inflation surged above 8%, the highest since the 1980s, due to increased demand and supply chain issues.

list.title: Current Situation:
list.snippet: As of June 2025, core inflation is at 2.70%.

list.title: Demand and Supply:
list.snippet: Changes in demand and supply, both domestic and global, significantly influence inflation rates.

list.title: Bank of Canada's Role:
list.snippet: The Bank of Canada plays a crucial role in managing inflation by adjusting interest rates.

list.title: Impact on Canadians:
list.snippet: High inflation can negatively impact those on fixed incomes and reduce purchasing power.

list.title: Economic Recovery:
list.snippet: The economic recovery after the pandemic, coupled with supply chain disruptions, contributed to the recent surge in inflation.

text_blocks.snippet: In summary, while Canada has experienced periods of high inflation, particularly during and after major events, it has generally maintained a low and stable inflation rate, targeted around 2%, through the efforts of the Bank of Canada and its management of the economy.
